name: @smileid/sample-ui
description: Every screen a partner sees, as pure TypeScript. Never published: the SDK repos consume this from source.

pinRationale.@smileid/usesmileid: peer, not a dependency: the host resolves the SDK so one UI source compiles against the published artifact here and against SDK HEAD in the SDK repo. Nothing imports it yet — the flow host is the next tranche — but the peer contract is what the SDK repos substitute against.
pinRationale.react: peer at the floor the SDK itself declares, so the host's copy is the only React in the tree.
pinRationale.react-native: peer; the version travels with the host app, never with a library.
pinRationale.react-native-svg: peer; the design's marks are SVG and the SDK already requires this package.
pinRationale.zustand: peer; the stores are app-lifetime state and the host decides when they are created.
pinRationale.@react-native/jest-preset: Required by peer from both react-native and jest-expo, and matched to the react-native version.
pinRationale.@testing-library/react-native: Renders a component and reads its resolved styles, which is what the token assertions need.
pinRationale.@types/jest: Matched to the jest 29 family below.
pinRationale.@types/react: Matched to the react the host pins, or JSX types disagree between the two packages.
pinRationale.jest: 29.7.0, not 30: jest-expo 57 depends on the jest 29 family (jest-snapshot, babel-jest, @jest/globals), and mixing a 30 runner with a 29 snapshot serialiser is how every golden reds at once.
pinRationale.jest-expo: Versioned with the Expo SDK; supplies the React Native transform and module mocks.
pinRationale.test-renderer: The modern replacement react-test-renderer became; @testing-library/react-native 14 requires it by peer.
pinRationale.typescript: 6.0.3, the version Expo SDK 57 expects. It also satisfies typescript-eslint 8's `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`, so type-aware linting stays on — 7.x would not.
pinRationale.@types/node: The test files read spec/ from disk, which needs the Node globals; nothing in src/ uses them.
pinRationale.react-native-safe-area-context: peer; the app bar reads the real status-bar inset rather than a constant, which is the rule insets stay platform-native.
pinRationale.@expo/ui: peer; the bottom sheet is the platform's own (SwiftUI sheet, Material3 ModalBottomSheet), which spec/components.json requires rather than a hand-rolled one. Already in the graph via expo-router.
pinRationale.react-native-gesture-handler: peer; the row swipe is the platform's own gesture, which spec/components.json requires rather than reproducing Android's velocity and threshold by hand.
pinRationale.@react-native-async-storage/async-storag: peer; the six settings are preferences and live where an uninstall clears them, apart from the token session. Already an optional peer of the SDK itself.
pinRationale.yoga-layout: The layout engine React Native itself lays out with, as its published WASM build. A hostless runner performs no layout at all, so the no-clipping predicate had no widths to judge text against and could only ever be a snapshot; this makes the box half of that measurement the real engine rather than a model of one.
pinRationale.@napi-rs/canvas: The pixel goldens' rasteriser: prebuilt Skia with no browser and no system libraries, so a jest worker paints the laid-out tree itself. Skia's PNG encoder is also what writes each baseline, since pngjs took seconds a screen.
pinRationale.pixelmatch: Compares a painted golden against its baseline at threshold 0 and writes the diff image a failure uploads.
pinRationale.pngjs: Decodes a baseline into raw pixels for the comparator, and encodes the diff image; nothing on the passing path uses it.
pinRationale.@types/pngjs: Types for pngjs, which ships none; pixelmatch ships its own.
